world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Tagdal is not in the catalog. The single Glottolog title item (Nicolaï 1980, 'Le songhay septentrional (études prosodiques)') could not be obtained online (HAL notice without file; not on Google Books, archive.org, HathiTrust or Gallica) and remains print only, priority high. However its content is reproduced first-hand in two open works by the same author downloaded in this search of works with stress in the title: Nicolaï's 1979 thesis (HAL tel-03112733; p. 48 'Type 3: système accentuel à liberté complète' for the nomad group, p. 324 'fort accent d'intensité, qualitativement identique à celui de la tamacheq', p. 327 initial-stress ['---] pattern in Tuareg loans in tihiʃit = Tagdal) and its published version, Nicolaï 1982 SAL 13(3): 273-322 (pp. 281, 304, 306, with the Tagdalt dialect listed under Tihiʃit on p. 314). These agree with the best statement, Benítez-Torres 2021 sec. 2.5: lexical, unpredictable stress, penult/final in disyllables, penult/antepenult (rarely final) in longer words, never before the antepenult. Recommended coding for a new record: lexical/free stress (stress-accent, no tone), bounded to the last three syllables.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is lexically specified and not predictable from shape, but confined to a right-edge three-syllable window: disyllables are penult- or final-stressed; words of three or more syllables are penult- or antepenult-stressed (final stress rare), never earlier than the antepenult. In Tuareg-origin vocabulary stress stays on its root syllable under affixation unless that would put it left of the antepenult, in which case it moves to the antepenult; antepenultimate stress triggers lengthening of the penult vowel and consonant. Songhay-origin nouns move stress onto plural -én. No lexical tone (unlike Tasawaq).
new_statements.exceptions: Clitics and bound morphemes almost never stressed except some Causative, Passive and Reciprocal prefixes; a few 3+-syllable words with final stress (əddəkúd, hinʃiiní, matalxér, mǝzzuurú); footnoted irregular items (taddǝ́but 'bed' shifts to antepenult in plural; táraywat, taʃʃát); speakers manipulate stress for riddles/jokes; stress 'tends to shift in different contexts' (morphology, sec. 3.1.2).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about isolated roots/citation forms ('how stress functions in isolated roots'); morphologically complex words treated in 3.1.2 (window restriction and shift to antepenult; shift to suffix -én/-yén). Phonetic correlates given as higher pitch and stronger airstream (borrowed wording from Christiansen-Bolli 2010:44 on Tadaksahak). Author attributes the 'lexical' characterisation to Nicolaï 1980 (études prosodiques) but the data and window generalisations are his own.
new_statements.identity_note: Benitez-Torres 2021 describes Tagdal as spoken in central Niger (Tahoua-Abalak-Agadez region); corpus of 45 texts from seven male speakers of the Kel Amdid/Tarbun, Kel Illokkod, Abargan varieties plus one Tabarog speaker (Tabarog, the Ibarogan variety, is treated as a dialect of Tagdal; differences said to be mainly segmental). Matches glottocode tagd1238 / ISO tda directly.

new_statements.citation: Benítez-Torres, Carlos M. (2021). A grammar of Tagdal: a Northern Songhay language. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden (LOT 608), sec. 2.5 'Stress', pp. 33-36.
new_statements.reading: Tagdal has lexical (free, unpredictable) word stress: disyllables penult or final, longer words penult or antepenult (rarely final), never further left than the antepenult; morphology shifts it (plural -én attracts stress; Tuareg-origin roots keep root stress unless pushed left of the antepenult). This is the most authoritative first-hand statement read. The new first-hand finds of this search of works with stress in the title are Nicolaï's 1979 thesis (p. 48, p. 324-327) and its 1982 SAL version (pp. 281, 304, 306), which underlie the 'lexical stress' claim: a 'système accentuel à liberté complète' in the nomad group (Tadaksahak, Tihiʃit = Tagdal) with a strong Tuareg-like intensity accent, stress permitted on the initial syllable of trisyllables and on the first syllable of four-syllable Tuareg loans. The two agree.

sources.quote: p. 281: "Type 3: Système accentuel à liberté complète. Ce système existe dans le songhay septentrional du groupe nomade. sources.note: Same first-hand content as the thesis, in the published journal version with a usable text layer: the nomadic Northern Songhay group (Tadaksahak and Tihiʃit = Tagdal; p. 314 lists 'X. Cites the unobtained Nicolaï 1980a as the source for the Type 3 statement.

sources.note: First-hand (Nicolaï's own fieldwork; 'Tihiʃit' is his name for Tagdal — the 1982 dialect list puts 'Tagdalt' and 'Tabarog' under Tihiʃit). Tagdal/Tadaksahak have a stress-accent system (no tones), a strong intensity accent like Tuareg's, with lexically free placement: unlike Eastern Songhay (final or penult only), stress may fall on the initial syllable of trisyllables and even on the first of four syllables in Tuareg loans (ˈtasaga, ˈtakazza, ˈso:rotan, ˈma:tiga).
